title: В Україні представили візуальний навігаційний модуль OSCAR, що забезпечує стійкість дронів до РЕБ
summary: English: 'Ukraine unveils the OSCAR visual navigation module that makes drones resilient to EW'. Twist Robotics' OSCAR (Optical System of Coordinates with Automatic Relocalization) recognises terrain landmarks in camera frames, matches them to a map, computes coordinates and passes them to the autopilot. Vendor claims: up to 20 m accuracy, day and night, over 500,000 km flown in 24 months, development aided by an in-house combat simulator ('Obrii').
key_takeaways: Map-matching visual positioning is fielded as an autopilot position source, not as a research demo
Vendor accuracy claim is ~20 m, which sets a realistic bar for hackathon VPS demos
Simulation of combat conditions is part of the development loop
Interfaces, weight and supported autopilots are not stated

title: Компанія, що постачає CRPA-антени для російських дронів, показала нову 32-елементну модель
summary: English: 'Company supplying CRPA antennas for Russian drones shows a new 32-element model'. Explains CRPA (controlled reception pattern antenna) as a multi-element array with digital beamforming that nulls interference directions while keeping satellite signals, and lists vendor specs of a 32-element Harxon unit shown at DWC2026 (up to 31 simultaneous interferers, under 6.5 kg, up to 90 W).
key_takeaways: CRPA element count is escalating (4 => 16 => 24 => 32) as an arms race against jamming
An N-element array can null up to N-1 interference sources
Size, weight and power of high-element CRPAs limit them to larger airframes
Explains why broadband jamming alone is losing effectiveness against long-range UAVs

title: Brave1 запускає лабораторію для тестування CRPA-антен
summary: English: 'Brave1 launches a lab for testing CRPA antennas'. Ukraine's defense-tech cluster opened a lab with EW equipment where domestic developers can test anti-jam GNSS antenna prototypes against jamming and get feedback before fielding. Test procedures are not described.
key_takeaways: Ukraine treats anti-jam GNSS antennas as a domestic product category with a dedicated test facility
Testing against real EW emitters is the gate before field use
Shows the government-cluster model (Brave1) for EW-resilience hardware

title: «Інколи від РЕБ очікують більше, ніж вона може». Як радіоелектронна боротьба працює проти FPV і «Шахедів»
summary: English: 'Sometimes more is expected from EW than it can deliver. How electronic warfare works against FPVs and Shaheds'. Explainer for engineers on defensive EW: control uplink, video downlink and GNSS as separate attack surfaces, why radio reconnaissance must precede jamming, why spoofing is weaker against drones with CRPA antennas and position-jump filters, and why fiber-optic and vision-autonomous drones bypass RF EW.
key_takeaways: Detection/RF reconnaissance comes before any effective jamming; protocols and frequencies shift often
Plausibility filters on position jumps plus CRPA blunt GNSS spoofing
Fiber-optic and onboard-vision drones remove the RF link entirely, so layered defense (EW + interceptors + fire) is the field answer
Friendly-fire on own drones is a real cost of EW

title: Як модернізуються «Шахеди» і чи є там штучний інтелект. Розбір DOU
summary: English: 'How Shaheds are being upgraded and whether there is AI inside. DOU breakdown'. Threat-side view of a long-range one-way UAV's navigation stack, useful for defenders: satellite navigation plus INS on pre-planned routes, 16-element CRPA antennas for jam/spoof resistance, and cellular modems used as trackers rather than as a navigation link.
key_takeaways: Upgraded long-range UAVs combine GNSS, INS and CRPA, which reduces the value of GNSS jamming as a defense
Cellular modems are telemetry/tracking aids, not navigation
Defensive conclusion in the article: interceptors outperform EW against these threats

title: «Ми почали будувати захищену екосистему для всіх військових застосунків». Архітектор DELTA - про розвиток системи
summary: English: 'We started building a secure ecosystem for all military applications. DELTA's architect on the system's development'. Interview on Ukraine's DELTA situational-awareness system: a shared core fed by aerial recon, satellites, drones and radars; a map as one view; a synchronization matrix linking drone missions to map objects; streaming, chat with zone alerts, mobile app, AI video detection; security built on NIST 800-53 and FIDO2.
key_takeaways: SA systems in Ukraine evolved from a single map into a product ecosystem on a common data core
Contrasted with the NATO model of separate systems joined by custom integration
Security baseline cited: NIST 800-53 and FIDO2 phishing-resistant auth
Offline/edge operation is not discussed

title: Шукають РЕБ/РЕР рішення для боротьби з ворожими дронами. Деталі про Jammer Hackathon
summary: English: 'EW/ELINT solutions against enemy drones wanted: Jammer Hackathon details'. Problem statement of the Brave1 + D3 Jammer Hackathon (29 Nov - 1 Dec 2024, $100k pool). Tracks: disrupting commercial-class drones via their control protocols, and automatic drone detection and tracking.
key_takeaways: Counter-UAS detection and tracking was an explicit hackathon track
Organisers named concrete commercial reference drones, so problem statements are platform-specific
Shows the typical Brave1 hackathon format: short sprint, jury pitch, follow-on funding

title: Завершився Jammer Hackathon, де шукали РЕБ/РЕР рішення для фронту. Які проєкти перемогли
summary: English: 'Jammer Hackathon is over: which EW/ELINT projects won'. Results page: winners include a reactive EW system, an FPV video-signal detector, and a radio-monitoring / direction-finding decision-support system (SPRMT); prizes $20k/$10k/$7k with a further $50k for one-month progress.
key_takeaways: Winning themes cluster around detection, direction finding and decision support, not only jamming
Short one-line descriptions only; no technical depth published
Follow-on prize for progress after a month is part of the format

title: У 17 років створив навігацію для дронів, яку не глушить РЕБ. Історія киянина, який переміг на «Олімпіаді геніїв» у США
summary: English: 'Built EW-proof drone navigation at 17: the story of a Kyiv student who won the Genius Olympiad in the USA'. Describes an urban GNSS-free concept: an IMU dead-reckons, side-looking rangefinders measure distances to buildings at roughly 7th-floor height, and the ranges are matched to OpenStreetMap building geometry about once per second. Simulation in C#/MonoGame; hardware tests on a Betaflight FPV were at bench stage.
key_takeaways: Rangefinder-to-building matching against OSM is a cheap urban alternative to camera VPS
Correction at ~1 Hz bounds IMU drift
Status at publication: simulation plus bench tests, not flight-proven

title: Vyriy створила маякову навігацію для дронів, яка працює без GPS і зв’язку
summary: English: 'Vyriy built beacon navigation for drones that works without GPS or a data link'. Ground radio beacons placed along a route in advance; an onboard board ranges to several beacons by delay or signal strength and trilaterates, like a local terrestrial GNSS. Frequencies, range and accuracy are not disclosed.
key_takeaways: Local terrestrial ranging beacons are a fielded GNSS substitute in Ukraine
Works without any link to the operator once the route is confirmed
No performance numbers published

title: Троє 20-річних хлопців за 24 години створили дрон, якому не потрібен GPS
summary: English: 'Three 20-year-olds built a drone that needs no GPS in 24 hours'. Ukrainian retelling (citing Defense One) of a US hackathon-born build motivated by Ukrainian front-line feedback: downward camera frames matched to stored imagery, ~256 GB of compressed map tiles covering 10,000+ sq km on an SD card, under $500 of hardware.
key_takeaways: Hackathon-scale VPS is feasible with commodity compute and pre-loaded tiles
Map storage and preloading time are the practical bottlenecks
Body text says several days of work, not 24 hours; open problems are altitude and speed envelope

title: 12 переможців і призовий фонд у 120 000 доларів: результати Хакатону «Наступ машин»
summary: English: '12 winners and a $120,000 prize pool: results of the Onslaught of Machines hackathon'. Official MoD results page: 2,000+ applications, 450 participants, 12 winners at $10k each. Winning-idea areas include advanced navigation systems, resilient communications, real-time recon data transfer, coordination of unmanned systems and network integration of heterogeneous unmanned systems.
key_takeaways: Navigation and resilient comms were named winning areas at a state-run drone hackathon
Judging criteria: deployment readiness, scalability, timeline
Winners are not named on the page

title: European Defense Tech Hackathon: Як стартапи в Мюнхені вирішують проблеми оборони України
summary: English: 'European Defense Tech Hackathon: how startups in Munich tackle Ukraine's defense problems'. Report from the Feb 2025 Munich edition (48 h, 200+ participants). Tracks included machine vision for counter-drone use, autonomous underwater navigation and improved radio reconnaissance. Brave1's stated expectation: integrable components, not finished systems.
key_takeaways: Hackathon outputs are valued as quickly integrable components
Underwater navigation appeared as a track
Teams, networks and investor access are the main realistic outcomes of 48 h

title: Боротьба за координати. Глобальні навігаційні системи та їх значення у сучасних військових конфліктах
summary: English: 'The fight for coordinates. GNSS and its role in modern military conflicts'. Pre-invasion (Jan 2022) Ukrainian overview of GNSS dependence, documented Russian interference during exercises in the Nordics/Baltics and Crimea, and responses: multi-constellation receivers, modernised GPS signals, quantum navigation research.
key_takeaways: Baseline for how the GNSS-interference picture looked just before 2022
Multi-constellation use is the first-line civilian mitigation
Good intro context for non-specialists

title: Алгоритм оптичної навігації дрона
summary: English: 'Drone optical navigation algorithm'. Master's defense slides (Kyiv-Mohyla Academy): a GeoTIFF map is cut into field-of-view tiles with precomputed keypoints; each drone frame is matched (ORB vs SuperPoint+SuperGlue) against tiles near the current estimate, a homography gives position, and fallback strategies handle lost or repeating fixes. Reported on 930 tiles: SuperPoint+SuperGlue reached the goal in fewer steps with more matches but ~631 s run time vs ~26 s for ORB; goal reached in 30/30 runs.
key_takeaways: Tile pre-indexing plus local search around the last fix is the practical VPS structure
Learned matchers win on match count but cost ~25x run time in this setup
Explicit fallback behaviours (repeat detection, default heading) matter as much as the matcher
Motivation cites both EW and fiber-optic range limits

title: Метод навігації БПЛА в умовах відсутності GPS-сигналу на основі візуальної одометрії
summary: English: 'UAV navigation method in GPS-denied conditions based on visual odometry'. Short Ukrainian conference paper: ORB features, a modified RANSAC and Kalman refinement for frame-to-frame VO, targeting +/-5 m and 10 Hz. Authors report 4.8 m position error (33% better than their baseline) and 42 ms per frame on a 10,000-frame closed-loop flight set.
key_takeaways: Sets a concrete target spec (+/-5 m, +/-2 deg, >=10 Hz) typical of Ukrainian academic work
Classic ORB + RANSAC + KF pipeline, not learned features
Results are the authors'; dataset not published

title: Інтелектуальна кіберфізична система для навігації БПЛА в умовах дії засобів РЕБ противника
summary: English: 'Intelligent cyber-physical system for UAV navigation under enemy EW'. Journal article fusing IMU data with optical-flow cameras via an EKF to hold position without any external radio signal, with a comparison of sparse (Lucas-Kanade), dense (Farneback) and learned (RAFT) optical flow.
key_takeaways: Side-by-side of LK, Farneback and RAFT for UAV flow is a handy reference
EKF remains the default fusion choice in Ukrainian applied work
Framed explicitly around full loss of external RF

title: Система управління та навігації БПЛА
summary: English: 'UAV control and navigation system'. KPI authors describe an ArduPilot-based control and navigation architecture intended to keep working under EW: protected GPS module, inertial navigation, backup channels, and ArduPilot code modifications including pseudo-random frequency reassignment for the link.
key_takeaways: Ukrainian practice modifies ArduPilot rather than writing autopilots from scratch
Link resilience (frequency agility) is treated together with navigation resilience
System-level description; limited quantitative evaluation

title: Комбіноване керування безпілотними літальними апаратами в умовах радіоелектронної боротьби
summary: English: 'Combined UAV control under electronic warfare'. Lviv Polytechnic article proposing a fiber-optic outbound leg plus anti-jam radio return leg, EO/IR fusion, and GNSS-free navigation with visual-inertial and lidar odometry corrected by baro and magnetometer, switched by a deterministic state machine. Reports prototype results over a 40 km mission (author figures: drift under 0.7%, 96% success over 50 runs).
key_takeaways: Mixed fiber + radio links appear as an EW-resilience pattern in Ukrainian research
Deterministic mode switching between nav sources is emphasised
Numbers are self-reported prototype results

title: Шляхи підвищення стійкості управління безпілотним літальним апаратом у завадовій обстановці
summary: English: 'Ways to increase UAV control resilience in a jamming environment'. Survey-style article from the National Guard Academy: optical/landmark navigation, hybrid GPS+optics, lidar, wideband data links, swarm concepts and adaptive signal processing as resilience levers.
key_takeaways: Readable Ukrainian-language map of the resilience options considered by practitioners
Lists landmark-based optical navigation systems as a key direction
Survey, not new results

title: Помехи в глобальных навигационных спутниковых системах
summary: English: 'Interference in global navigation satellite systems'. Habr article by a developer of interference-resistant receivers: why GNSS is below the noise floor, receiver structure (front end, 1-2 bit sampling, per-satellite correlator channels), narrowband vs wideband jamming and spoofing, and their effect on code/carrier tracking loops.
key_takeaways: Clear receiver-level explanation of how jamming breaks tracking loops
Low-bit quantization trades SNR for simpler correlators, which matters under jamming
Anti-jam methods were deferred to a part 2

title: GPS: глушилки, спуфинг и уязвимости
summary: English: 'GPS: jammers, spoofing and vulnerabilities'. Early Russian-language overview: how spoofing gradually walks a receiver off, the 2013 UT Austin yacht demonstration, consumer jammers sold in Russia, lab results on car jammers, and proposed defenses. The comment thread adds practitioner views (TERCOM as a GPS backup, antenna shielding limits).
key_takeaways: Gradual pull-off is the core spoofing technique
Cheap personal jammers were already widespread years before 2022
Comments are a source of practitioner folklore, not verified data

title: SDR приемник GPS на микроконтроллере
summary: English: 'SDR GPS receiver on a microcontroller'. Builds a real-time software GPS receiver on an STM32F4 (later ESP32) fed with 1-bit samples from a MAX2769 front end: XOR-based correlation, table bit-sums, four time-multiplexed channels with DLL/PLL, navigation decoding, RTCM 3 pseudorange output and on-chip RTKLIB positioning (author reports ~80 m indoors).
key_takeaways: A GPS receiver can run on a commodity MCU without FPGA
Exposes the tracking loops that interference attacks
Good hands-on companion to receiver-theory articles

title: Высокоточная навигация GNSS RTK
summary: English: 'High-precision GNSS RTK navigation'. Hands-on review of the u-blox ZED-F9P: tracing letters and spinning the antenna on a carousel to visualise RTK Fixed track quality. Comments add practical limits (lower RTK rate with more constellations, LoRa correction links, urban canyon dropouts).
key_takeaways: Simple visual tests (carousel, letters) expose RTK fix quality without survey gear
RTK output rate drops with the number of constellations
Comment thread has DIY base-station experience

title: RTKLib - Сантиметровая точность GPS/ГЛОНАСС в пост-обработке
summary: English: 'RTKLIB: centimeter-level GPS/GLONASS accuracy in post-processing'. Step-by-step base (rooftop) + rover logging with two raw-capable receivers and processing with STRSVR, RTKCONV and RTKPOST in kinematic mode; author reports fixed solutions for 97.3% of epochs.
key_takeaways: Complete RTKLIB post-processing walk-through in Russian
GLONASS enabled alongside GPS
Useful for building ground truth for nav experiments

title: Как я научил квадрокоптер возвращаться домой без GPS: алгоритм «верёвочной лестницы»
authors: Habr author (name not verified; companion repo by VohminV)
summary: English: 'How I taught a quadcopter to return home without GPS: the rope-ladder algorithm'. Explains why integrating optical flow velocity drifts so that the drone ends up offset after return, and replaces it with stored keyframe 'rungs' matched on the way back. Habr blocked automated fetch, so author and date are not verified (year inferred from the companion repo, created July 2025); content summarised from search snippets and the repo README.
key_takeaways: Flow integration error accumulates; keyframe matching bounds it for return-home
Teach-and-repeat is a pragmatic answer when only the way back matters

title: Уловки, подсмотренные у медоносных пчёл, помогают дронам возвращаться домой без GPS
summary: English: 'Tricks borrowed from honeybees help drones return home without GPS'. Russian translation of a New Atlas piece on TU Delft's Bee-Nav: after a short exploratory flight capturing panoramas, a tiny network (3.4 KB indoors, 42 KB outdoors) estimates direction and distance home. Reported outdoor runs exceeded 600 m, with ~70% success in wind.
key_takeaways: Homing can be learned with kilobyte-size models
Wind tilt degrades panoramic matching
Shows Russian tech media tracking GNSS-free homing closely

title: Навигация без GPS, которая уже работает
summary: English: 'Navigation without GPS that already works'. Overview of deployed or demonstrated non-GNSS methods: accelerometer-based subway positioning, a star-tracker drone prototype (Raspberry Pi 5, night only, ~4 km accuracy), quantum-magnetometer map matching (AQNav), quantum accelerometers, and barometric tunnel detection.
key_takeaways: Broad menu of alternative PNT methods with honest limits (night-only, km-level)
Magnetic anomaly navigation is presented as the most mature quantum-sensing use

title: Навигация квадрокоптера с использованием монокулярного зрения
summary: English: 'Quadcopter navigation using monocular vision'. Walk-through of monocular navigation on a Parrot AR.Drone: building an obstacle map from a single camera and correcting the trajectory.
key_takeaways: Early Russian-language introduction to monocular VO/SLAM on a toy platform
Scale ambiguity and obstacle mapping are the central difficulties

title: Технология коррекции навигационных параметров БПЛА в условиях отсутствия сигналов спутниковой навигации с использованием методов оптической одометрии
summary: English: 'Technology for correcting UAV navigation parameters without satellite signals using optical odometry'. Short competition paper from Russia's state aviation systems institute on correcting micro-multicopter navigation with optical odometry when GNSS is absent, framed by autonomy-level roadmaps.
key_takeaways: Shows GNSS-denied optical odometry was an institutional priority in Russia by 2016
Framed around small multicopters

title: Навигация по снимкам местности на основе сопоставления глубоких признаков и визуальной одометрии
summary: English: 'Terrain relative navigation based on deep feature template matching and visual odometry'. Belarusian journal article: self-supervised (triplet-loss) deep features for matching UAV views to satellite patches across season, weather and lighting; visual odometry bridges featureless forest/field areas; an entropy filter plus path planning steers flights over feature-rich terrain.
key_takeaways: Plan the route over informative terrain instead of only improving the matcher
Self-supervised features avoid labelled cross-season data
VO bridges texture-poor segments between absolute fixes

title: Разработка алгоритма абсолютной визуально-инерциальной навигации беспилотных воздушных судов
summary: English: 'Development of an absolute visual-inertial navigation algorithm for unmanned aircraft'. Russian preprint comparing absolute navigation methods against preloaded satellite maps and proposing a season-invariant SIFT keypoint matching approach corrected by INS, optimised for real time and evaluated on real flight data against GNSS reference. Year inferred from the PDF (references run to 2025).
key_takeaways: Absolute map-based fixes + INS is the mainstream Russian approach too
Seasonal invariance is the named key problem
Evaluated against GNSS reference on real flights

title: Алгоритм планирования маршрута БПЛА в условиях недостатка визуальных ориентиров
summary: English: 'UAV route planning algorithm under a shortage of visual landmarks'. Journal article (Analysis and Data Processing Systems, vol. 94 no. 2) on planning routes so a video-navigation system keeps seeing enough landmarks when satellite navigation is unavailable.
key_takeaways: Navigation-aware path planning: route choice is a resilience lever
Pairs naturally with map-matching VPS that fails over texture-poor areas

title: GPS complex interference models and the possible antispoofing protective measures
summary: Belarusian conference paper (BSUIR, 'Information radiosystems and radiotechnologies 2022'; English title, Russian-language repository) on GPS interference models and possible anti-spoofing protections. Only the metadata was checked; conclusions not verified.
key_takeaways: Example of the Belarusian academic literature on spoofing defences
Metadata only verified

title: Неоднозначный сигнал
summary: English: 'An ambiguous signal'. Russian-language independent journalism on GNSS interference over Europe: cites an EU states' report to ICAO (about 123k affected flights in Jan-Apr 2025), Estonian, Lithuanian and Polish statistics, jamming vs spoofing mechanics, and trackers such as gpsjam.org and gpswise.aero.
key_takeaways: Interference has spilled far beyond the front line into civil aviation
Spoofing shows up as position jumps of hundreds of km and inconsistent instrument readings
Public trackers are the main open data sources cited

title: Навигация по Optical Flow · Clover
summary: English: 'Optical Flow navigation - Clover docs'. Russian-language official documentation for enabling downward-camera optical flow on the Clover quadcopter (requires a laser rangefinder), the ROS topics involved and the PX4 EKF2/flow parameters to set, plus tuning advice. Year approximate (docs are continuously updated).
key_takeaways: Concrete parameter list for optical-flow-only position hold in PX4
Rangefinder is mandatory for metric flow
Max horizontal speed is limited in flow mode

title: Навигация по карте маркеров · Clover
summary: English: 'Navigation by marker map - Clover docs'. Russian documentation for flying with a map of ArUco markers (floor or ceiling), publishing the resulting pose to the flight controller as a vision position estimate, and commanding flights in the marker-map frame. Year approximate.
key_takeaways: Fiducial maps are the fastest way to get GNSS-free indoor positioning for a demo
Shows the generic pattern: external pose => VPE => autopilot EKF

title: CopterHack 2023
summary: Russian-language page of COEX's international open-source flying-robotics contest built on the Clover platform: format (teams develop open-source projects over months with expert feedback), final standings and links to projects, including a radio-navigation system entry.
key_takeaways: Open-source requirement makes finalist repos reusable
Long-format contest, unlike 48 h hackathons
Navigation and swarm entries recur across editions
